**Business Rule:**

- Vowels are: a, e, i, o, u.
- Every other alphabet character is considered a consonant.

tickets.title: Ticket 4 — Standardize Employee IDs for HR Reports
tickets.description:
The Human Resources (HR) department receives employee IDs from multiple legacy systems. Some systems store the IDs in lowercase letters, while the reporting system requires every employee ID to be displayed in uppercase for consistency.

Your task is to write a program that converts all lowercase characters in an employee ID to uppercase **without using any built-in string conversion functions**.

**Business Rule:**
- Convert every lowercase English letter (`a-z`) to its uppercase equivalent (`A-Z`).
- Do not use built-in functions such as `upper()`.
- Characters that are already uppercase or non-alphabetic should remain unchanged.

A secure messaging platform applies a lightweight encryption technique before transmitting customer messages over the network. Instead of changing the order of the words, the system encrypts each word individually by reversing its characters. This makes the message less readable while preserving the original sentence structure.

Your task is to write a program that reverses every word in a given sentence while keeping the order of the words unchanged.

**Business Rules:**
- Reverse the characters of each word individually.
- Preserve the original word order.
- Words are separated by a single space.

tickets.title: Ticket 8 — Identify the First Unique Transaction ID
tickets.description:
A fintech company processes millions of payment transactions every day. During log analysis, each transaction is represented by a sequence of characters. Due to retries and duplicate processing, many transaction identifiers appear multiple times. The fraud detection team needs to identify the **first unique transaction identifier** in the sequence to trace the original successful transaction.

Your task is to write a program that finds the **first non-repeating character** in a given transaction log.

**Business Rules:**
- Return the first character that appears exactly once.
- Preserve the original order while checking.
- If every character repeats, return **-1**.

tickets.title: Ticket 9 — Verify Duplicate Customer Accounts
tickets.description:
A banking application imports customer records from multiple legacy systems. Sometimes the same customer's name is entered with the letters rearranged, causing duplicate accounts to be created.

To prevent duplicate customer profiles, the system must determine whether two customer names contain exactly the same characters with the same frequency, regardless of their order.

Your task is to write a program that checks whether two given strings represent the same set of characters.

**Business Rules:**
- Two customer names are considered duplicates if they contain exactly the same characters with the same frequency.
- Character order does not matter.
- If both strings satisfy the above condition, print **Anagram**; otherwise print **Not Anagram**.

tickets.title: Ticket 12 — Compress Sensor Data Before Cloud Upload
tickets.description:
An IoT platform collects millions of readings from smart devices every minute. Since network bandwidth is limited, the edge device must compress the sensor data before sending it to the cloud.

The compression algorithm stores each character followed by the number of consecutive times it appears. This reduces the amount of data transmitted while preserving the original information.

Your task is to write a program that compresses a string using **Run-Length Encoding (RLE)**.

**Business Rules:**
- Consecutive identical characters should be replaced by the character followed by its count.
- If a character appears only once, include the count as **1**.
- Maintain the original order of characters.

tickets.title: Ticket 13 — Detect the Longest Stable Network Session
tickets.description:
A cybersecurity monitoring system analyzes a continuous stream of user session events. Each character in the event stream represents an action performed by a user.

For security analytics, engineers need to identify the **longest continuous session** in which **no action is repeated**. Repeated actions may indicate loops, retries, or suspicious behavior, so the monitoring system measures the longest unique sequence of actions.

Your task is to write a program that finds the **length of the longest substring without repeating characters**.

**Business Rules:**
- Consider only contiguous characters (a substring).
- No character may appear more than once in the selected substring.
- Return only the length of the longest valid substring.

The monitoring system needs to verify whether a backup sequence received from a secondary server is simply a rotation of the original backup sequence.

Your task is to write a program to check whether one string is a rotation of another string.

**Business Rules:**
- Two sequences are considered rotated if one can be obtained by shifting characters of the other string.
- Both strings must contain the same characters with the same frequency.
- If the second sequence is not a valid rotation, return False.

tickets.title: Ticket 21 — Optimize Unique User Activity Sequence Detection
tickets.description:
A cybersecurity analytics platform monitors user activity logs to detect the longest continuous sequence of unique actions performed without repetition.

Each user activity session is represented as a string where every character represents an action event. The monitoring system needs to efficiently find the maximum length of a continuous activity sequence where no action is repeated.

The previous version of the system used a brute force approach, which became slow for large activity logs. The engineering team needs an optimized solution using a sliding window approach to improve performance.

Write a program to find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters using an optimized approach.
